1	---
2	name: code-review
3	description: "Review code changes adversarially for correctness and evidence, with an explicit check that tests, assertions, tolerances, comparators, labels, and gates were not weakened to make the change appear successful. Use whenever reviewing a diff, commit, pull request, test change, validation change, or dispatching an adversarial code review."
4	---
5	
6	# Code review
7	
8	## Purpose
9	
10	Try to refute the change's correctness claims. Inspect the implementation, its
11	tests, and the evidence together. A passing suite is not sufficient when the
12	change also weakens what the suite requires.
13	
14	This skill owns the substance of adversarial code review. Separate skills may
15	set reviewer counts, exact-head attestation, validation authority, and landing
16	policy.
17	
18	## Establish the review target
19	
20	Before reviewing, identify the repository, base revision, exact head revision,
21	and intended behavior. Review the complete diff and the relevant surrounding
22	code and tests. Bind the verdict to the exact head; a changed head requires a
23	fresh review.
24	
25	## Mandatory goalpost-moving check
26	
27	The coordinator applies this check before dispatching an adversarial review and
28	includes this complete block in every adversarial-review prompt, not a pointer
29	to it:
30	
31	> GOALPOST-MOVING REVIEW RULE
32	>
33	> Adversarial reviewers must look explicitly for goalpost moving. We are extremely skeptical of any goalpost moving. YOU DO NOT CLEAR THE BAR BY SIMPLY LOWERING THE BAR.
34	>
35	> Treat each of these as an explicit review target:
36	> - weakening an assertion so a test passes
37	> - widening a tolerance · adding an exemption · skipping a case · relaxing a comparator
38	> - renaming or relabelling so a failure reads as a pass
39	> - deleting a check rather than satisfying it
40	
41	Compare every changed test, threshold, allowlist, skip, label, classification,
42	and gate with the base revision. Determine whether the implementation now meets
43	the original requirement or whether the requirement was changed to admit the
44	implementation. Call out either result explicitly, including when no lowering
45	of the bar is present.
46	
47	## Review method
48	
49	1. Trace the changed behavior through the real execution path. Do not infer
50	   behavior from names, configuration, or successful exit status alone.
51	2. Check the claimed evidence against the exact behavior it is supposed to
52	   prove. Identify missing identity, causation, coverage, or provenance links.
53	3. Inspect production and test changes together. Require a qualifying case to
54	   pass and a violating case to be refused when the change introduces or alters
55	   a guard.
56	4. Report concrete findings with file and line evidence, impact, and the change
57	   required to resolve them. Do not substitute a vague procedural objection for
58	   a technical finding.
59	5. State a verdict only after resolving the goalpost-moving check and the
60	   correctness findings against the exact reviewed head.
61	
62	## Report structure
63	
64	```text
65	Review target: <repository> <base>..<exact head>
66

file.content:
---
name: code-review
description: "Review code changes adversarially for correctness and evidence, with an explicit check that tests, assertions, tolerances, comparators, labels, and gates were not weakened to make the change appear successful. Use whenever reviewing a diff, commit, pull request, test change, validation change, or dispatching an adversarial code review."
---

# Code review

## Purpose

Try to refute the change's correctness claims. Inspect the implementation, its
tests, and the evidence together. A passing suite is not sufficient when the
change also weakens what the suite requires.

This skill owns the substance of adversarial code review. Separate skills may
set reviewer counts, exact-head attestation, validation authority, and landing
policy.

## Establish the review target

Before reviewing, identify the repository, base revision, exact head revision,
and intended behavior. Review the complete diff and the relevant surrounding
code and tests. Bind the verdict to the exact head; a changed head requires a
fresh review.

## Mandatory goalpost-moving check

The coordinator applies this check before dispatching an adversarial review and
includes this complete block in every adversarial-review prompt, not a pointer
to it:

> GOALPOST-MOVING REVIEW RULE
>
> Adversarial reviewers must look explicitly for goalpost moving. We are extremely skeptical of any goalpost moving. YOU DO NOT CLEAR THE BAR BY SIMPLY LOWERING THE BAR.
>
> Treat each of these as an explicit review target:
> - weakening an assertion so a test passes
> - widening a tolerance · adding an exemption · skipping a case · relaxing a comparator
> - renaming or relabelling so a failure reads as a pass
> - deleting a check rather than satisfying it

Compare every changed test, threshold, allowlist, skip, label, classification,
and gate with the base revision. Determine whether the implementation now meets
the original requirement or whether the requirement was changed to admit the
implementation. Call out either result explicitly, including when no lowering
of the bar is present.

## Review method

1. Trace the changed behavior through the real execution path. Do not infer
   behavior from names, configuration, or successful exit status alone.
2. Check the claimed evidence against the exact behavior it is supposed to
   prove. Identify missing identity, causation, coverage, or provenance links.
3. Inspect production and test changes together. Require a qualifying case to
   pass and a violating case to be refused when the change introduces or alters
   a guard.
4. Report concrete findings with file and line evidence, impact, and the change
   required to resolve them. Do not substitute a vague procedural objection for
   a technical finding.
5. State a verdict only after resolving the goalpost-moving check and the
   correctness findings against the exact reviewed head.

## Report structure

```text
Review target: <repository> <base>..<exact head>

Findings:
- <severity>: <file:line> — <problem, impact, and required change>

Goalpost-moving assessment:
- Assertions weakened: yes/no — <evidence>
- Tolerance widened, exemption added, case skipped, or comparator relaxed: yes/no — <evidence>
- Failure renamed or relabelled as a pass: yes/no — <evidence>
- Check deleted instead of satisfied: yes/no — <evidence>

Verification: <commands or evidence inspected, with limitations>
Verdict: approve / changes requested
```

Put findings first. If there are no findings, say so explicitly and still
include the goalpost-moving assessment, residual risks, and verification limits.

4	
5	KVM synthesizes stable `/proc` files rather than exposing host process state. It covers all 17 fixed paths returned by `synthetic_proc_content` and already-supported readable dynamic fdinfo descriptions.
6	
7	This is a prerequisite for authenticated proc-carrier identity and `syncfs`; it does not implement either feature, SCM_RIGHTS identity transport, record/replay, or complete KVM parity.
8	
9	## Safety and determinism
10	
11	Each covered snapshot is fully populated, chmodded to 0444, and permanently sealed with `F_SEAL_WRITE | F_SEAL_GROW | F_SEAL_SHRINK | F_SEAL_SEAL` before publication. The kernel-added `F_SEAL_EXEC` shape is accepted; any other extra or missing seal fails closed. The writable construction descriptor never enters the guest table.
12	
13	Fixed snapshots get a newly reopened `O_RDONLY` or `O_PATH` description. Readable fdinfo snapshots get a newly reopened `O_RDONLY` description, preserve the modeled seq-file pwrite ordering, and keep their existing per-description lifecycle state. A non-`O_NOFOLLOW` allocation now explicitly removes stale virtual nofollow metadata for a reused descriptor number.
14	
15	## Linux semantics and v9 corrections
16	
17	The open path validates complete non-`O_PATH` `__O_TMPFILE` forms before pathname access and caches whether the host follows the pre-6.4 `LegacyLookup` or current `EarlyEinval` create-plus-directory policy.
18	
19	V9 corrects and tests the review findings against pinned Linux v6.3 source:
20	
21	- Existing `/proc/mounts` with `O_CREAT|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW` returns `ENOTDIR` under `LegacyLookup`, or `EEXIST` with `O_EXCL`; ordinary `/proc/mounts|O_NOFOLLOW` remains `ELOOP`.
22	- A missing, closed, or malformed nonempty fdinfo final component remains `ENOENT` for every `O_EXCL`/`O_NOFOLLOW` combination. Procfs supplies that terminal error before namei's create fallback.
23	- Exact `/proc/.../fdinfo/` with legacy `O_CREAT|O_DIRECTORY` returns `EISDIR`, including with `O_EXCL` or `O_NOFOLLOW`, after confirming the selected task is live.
24	- Live readable fdinfo pwrite is checked against native Linux: nonnegative offsets return `ESPIPE` before count or pointer validation; negative offsets return `EINVAL`; invalid descriptors retain the corresponding `EBADF`/`EINVAL` ordering.
25	- Native DAC-sensitive `EACCES`/`EPERM` comparisons are run only under a non-root supervisor. Guest immutability assertions remain unconditional, and the required-KVM guest proves its modeled uid/euid are zero before requiring `fchmod(...)=EPERM`.
26	
27	## Validation
28	
29	Every Cargo command used `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` and a 180-second outer timeout. Durations are whole-command wall times including compilation and linking.
30	
31	- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passed in 2.143 s
32	- focused synthetic-proc library tests: 33 passed, 0 failed in 23.205 s
33	- exact seal, fdinfo-carrier/pwrite, lifecycle-generation, and stale-nofollow controls: each passed
34	- required real-KVM static-ELF test with `REVERIE_REQUIRE_KVM=1`: 1 passed, 0 failed in 31.112 s; KVM absence cannot skip
35	- full `reverie-kvm` library: 815 passed, 0 failed in 13.905 s
36	- strict all-target Clippy: passed in 9.842 s
37	- expanded native matrices: passed in 0.232 s, including the seven-case fdinfo pwrite oracle
38	- four v9 causal source mutations each failed the intended literal assertion and restored all source and patch hashes
39	- `git diff --check`: passed
40	
41	The first full-library attempt had one unrelated concurrent pipe-test failure: `positioned_vectored_io_handles_pipes_partial_writes_and_sigpipe` observed a four-byte write instead of `EPIPE`. Its exact rerun passed, an immediate full retry passed 815/815, and the final post-mutation full suite passed 815/815. No source change was made for that flake.
42	
43	The full base-to-v9 binary patch SHA-256 is `ca2a95b12e6cdadfb3ac983c67aa21dd6fee6e9b7ac66271a7e7228732e5eb1e`. Validation ran on x86-64 Linux 7.1.3 as supervisor EUID 212630.
44	
45	## Explicit residuals and evidence limits
46	
47	- No Linux 5.8–6.3 runtime is available locally. Legacy behavior is supported by pinned upstream source, https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/43b450632676fb60e9faeddff285d9fac94a4f58, and injected exact tests, not claimed as locally executed.
48	- `/proc/self/loginuid`, deterministic random devices, and synthetic sysfs CPU-frequency files remain on the older generic virtual-file carrier. A representative control samples `/proc/self/loginuid`, `/dev/urandom`, and `/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/boost`, showing those three carriers are unsealed and can still be reopened through guest proc-fd as writable; this patch does not claim untested path coverage or fix the carrier class.
49	- Linux permits `O_PATH`, including `O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW`, on live fdinfo entries. Reverie still returns `ENOSYS`; fdinfo `O_PATH` lifecycle/link/status parity is out of scope. Bare fdinfo `O_CREAT`, `O_CREAT|O_EXCL`, `O_TRUNC`, and `O_DIRECT` ordering also remains a disclosed pre-existing mismatch.
50	- Exact `/proc/self/fdinfo/` ordinary-open/directory/TMPFILE behavior remains the pre-existing `ENOENT` residual; only its legacy create-directory ordering changes here.

53	- A future kernel-added implicit memfd seal other than `F_SEAL_EXEC` causes a deliberate `EOPNOTSUPP` fail-closed result.

This v9 head supersedes both exact-head verdicts and requires fresh Codex- and Claude-family adversarial approvals.

60	
61	Trigger 2: this changes Reverie's KVM syscall-interception behavior and guest-visible file-description semantics.
62	
63	Trigger 3: sealed synthetic proc carriers are a determinization mechanism for guest-visible kernel metadata. Independent exact-head Codex- and Claude-family adversarial approvals are required before landing.

    kvm: correct legacy proc flag precedence
    
    [hermit2, degraded-unresolved, gpt-5.6-sol, devbig014, role=impl]
    
    Correct pre-6.4 create-plus-directory ordering for /proc/mounts and
    dynamic fdinfo paths. Keep negative fdinfo leaves at ENOENT, distinguish
    the fdinfo directory trailing slash as EISDIR, and clear stale virtual
    O_NOFOLLOW state when a descriptor number is reused.
    
    Add native and guest pwrite ordering checks for fdinfo carriers, explicit
    seal and credential controls, and disclose the remaining generic-carrier
    and statx residuals.
    
    Tested with 33 focused synthetic-proc tests, one required real-KVM test,
    815 full reverie-kvm library tests, strict all-target Clippy, native open
    matrices, and four failing causal mutations.

# Adversarial review — rrnewton/reverie PR 609

Review target: `rrnewton/reverie` `b13ad926a34f27bb39a349429a1d08e812d741b4..33d8ee90c2ae81556e42345b3d05e37f088b9c04`, tree `4d9a7b3333dc791439449e3d6b9ee4aefc5572af`.

Packet identity checked before review: `BASE-TO-HEAD.patch` hashes to `ca2a95b1…5eb1e` as claimed in `INPUTS.json`, `SOURCE.json`, `qualification/v9/final-patch.sha256`, `pre-mutation.patch`, `post-report-base.patch`, and all four `proof-*.post-base.patch` files. `qualification/v9/final-source.sha256` is byte-identical to `SOURCE.json.source_sha256` and to the `candidate/` hashes in `INPUTS.json`. Independently of the filename or the report's heading, the patch's post-image blob IDs (`50e7cdd7`, `fc4a723a`, `8a672800`) match `primary/HEAD-TREE.txt` lines 2205/2213/2280 for `elf.rs`, `executor.rs`, `static_elf.rs` at the committed head, and `proof-frozen-executor.rs` hashes to the exact-head `executor.rs`. The v9 report's stale "v8 HEAD" heading is therefore cosmetic; the evidence is bound to this head by content.

---

## Findings

No high- or medium-severity correctness defect found in the sealed-carrier mechanism, the open-path ordering, or the fdinfo lifecycle. Five low/informational findings follow.

**1. Low — stale `synthetic_proc_nofollow_fds` cleanup covers only one of the descriptor allocators.**
`candidate/reverie-kvm/src/executor.rs:13195-13199` clears the stale marker only when `open_synthetic_proc` allocates. Every other allocator leaves it untouched: `insert_file_with_flags` (`executor.rs:7815-7846`), which backs `open_guest_fd_path` (`7522`), `open_virtual_file`, and pipe/socket creation; and `install_received_rights` (`executor.rs:10514-10521`), which explicitly does `proc_files.insert`/`remove` for the received fd but never touches the nofollow set. The `F_GETFL` overlay at `executor.rs:13570-13580` consults the set for *any* guest fd, not only proc carriers, so a stale entry would add a spurious `O_NOFOLLOW` to an unrelated description. Guest-visible impact if reachable: wrong `fcntl(F_GETFL)` for an arbitrary descriptor — deterministic, but wrong. I could **not** construct a reachable stale entry at this head: `close` (`13712-13717`), both `duplicate_fd` paths (`8079-8086`, `8100-8107`), `duplicate_fd_at_or_above` (`7980-7986`), and the exec filter (`elf.rs:1071-1075`) all clear or filter it, and `insert_file_with_flags` only selects vacant fds. Required correction: move the `remove` into `insert_file_with_flags` so every allocation path is covered, or state in the PR that the side table is consulted only for fds the synthetic-proc allocator owns. Not blocking.

**2. Low — the new host-kernel dependence of guest-visible errno is not in the disclosed residual list.**
`elf.rs:67-138` probes the host once and caches it; `executor.rs:7040-7046`, `212-227`, `2038-2046`, `7062-7078` then make the guest's errno for `O_CREAT|O_DIRECTORY` (`EINVAL` vs `ENOTDIR`/`EEXIST`) and for `/proc/.../fdinfo/` (`EINVAL` vs `EISDIR`) a function of the supervisor's kernel version. This is the only way to match native behavior, and the PR body says the policy is cached, but it is a genuinely new cross-host divergence surface: the same guest program yields different errnos on a 6.3 host and a 7.1 host. The PR's residual section otherwise enumerates nonclaims carefully and omits this one. Required correction: add it to the disclosed residuals. No code change needed (record/replay is explicitly out of scope).

**3. Low — a transient probe failure is cached permanently.**
`elf.rs:41-43` declares `OnceLock<Result<RegularCreateDirectoryPolicy, String>>` and `elf.rs:131` uses `get_or_init`, so an `Err` is stored forever. A single failure of `openat`/`fstat`/`fstatfs` on `/proc/self/status` — including exhausting `POLICY_OPEN_EINTR_ATTEMPTS = 16` at `elf.rs:31,49-64` — permanently disables every later `load_static_elf`/`load_static_elf_file` in the same supervisor process. It fails closed, and procfs `openat` is not realistically `EINTR`-interruptible, so this is near-unreachable; caching the failure is also arguably the right choice for determinism (the policy must not change mid-run). Required correction: state the permanent-poison behavior in a comment, or cache success only. Not blocking.

**4. Low — dead `/proc/uptime` branch that would build an unsealed carrier.**
`executor.rs:7155-7157` returns `open_virtual_file(state, b"0.00 0.00\n", …)` for `/proc/uptime`, but `synthetic_proc_content` handles `/proc/uptime` at `executor.rs:12890` and returns first, so the branch is unreachable. It is pre-existing, not introduced here, but it now silently contradicts the new invariant that all 17 fixed paths get a sealed carrier: were it ever reached it would hand the guest an unsealed, mode-0755 memfd. Required correction: delete the dead branch. Not blocking.

**5. Informational — the four headline v9 `LegacyLookup` corrections have no runtime oracle whatsoever.**
They are exercised only by unit tests that *inject* `RegularCreateDirectoryPolicy::LegacyLookup` into `state` (`executor.rs:29559-29560`, `29678-29679`, `31586`) and by the guest program's `if (expected_create_directory == ENOTDIR)` block (`tests/static_elf.rs`, patch lines 4798-4828) which **did not execute** on the `EarlyEinval` validation host. The unconditional native comparison in `synthetic_proc_direct_combined_open_matrix_preserves_policy_and_native_ordering` (`executor.rs:18958-18972`) is a real oracle for the mapping, but on this host it only ever exercises the `EINVAL` arm. The report discloses this honestly. I therefore checked the legacy claims against the pinned sources myself, and they hold:

- `linux/v6.3-fs-open.c:1156-1273` has no global `O_DIRECTORY|O_CREAT` rejection; `linux/v7.1-fs-open.c:1219-1225` does. Both call `build_open_flags` before `getname` (`v6.3:1332-1342`, `v7.1:1355-1364`), so placing the `EarlyEinval` check ahead of `read_c_string` at `executor.rs:7040` is correct, and the guest-test `EINVAL`-before-`EFAULT`/`EBADF`/`ENOENT` matrix (patch 4664-4681) is the right expectation.
- `linux/v6.3-fs-namei.c:3533-3544`: `O_EXCL` → `EEXIST` precedes `LOOKUP_DIRECTORY` → `ENOTDIR`, which precedes `may_open`'s `S_IFLNK` → `ELOOP` at `v6.3-fs-namei.c:3162-3164`. So `/proc/mounts|O_CREAT|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW` is `ENOTDIR` (not `ELOOP`), with `O_EXCL` it is `EEXIST`, and ordinary `/proc/mounts|O_NOFOLLOW` remains `ELOOP`. `synthetic_proc_create_directory_errno` (`executor.rs:212-227`) matches, and the v8 `ELOOP` it replaced was wrong.
- `linux/v6.3-fs-proc-fd.c:221-241` (`proc_lookupfd_common`) returns `ERR_PTR(-ENOENT)` directly for a missing, non-numeric, or leading-zero leaf; `v6.3-fs-namei.c:3393-3404` propagates it from `out_dput` **before** the `create_error` fallback at `3421-3424`, and `create_error` from `may_o_create` is never consulted because the dentry is negative only in the create branch. The earlier reviewer's proposed `EACCES` is refuted; `FdinfoPathTarget::MissingFinal` → `ENOENT` (`executor.rs:1984`, `7079-7080`) is correct.
- `v6.3-fs-namei.c:3466-3469` returns `-EISDIR` on the create side for a trailing slash, after the parent walk has already resolved `/proc/<pid>`, so gating `EISDIR` behind `fdinfo_task_generation` (`executor.rs:7063-7077`) is the correct order.

---

## Goalpost-moving assessment

**Assertions weakened: no.** I enumerated every `-` line in `BASE-TO-HEAD.patch`. The only removed test-body content is a relocation: `fdinfo_record_capacity_and_flags_validation_preserve_other_raw_fields` and the whole `FdinfoFixture` impl are removed at patch 4002-4330 and re-added byte-identically at patch 3534-3630 (same raw `pos:/flags:/mnt_id:/ino:/lock:` fixture string, same `EOVERFLOW`/`EIO` expectations, same helper bodies). One blank line is removed at patch 3521. `#[test]` count in `executor.rs` goes 281 → 306; `#[ignore]` and `should_panic` appear nowhere in the diff.

**Tolerance widened, exemption added, case skipped, or comparator relaxed: one exemption, narrowly scoped and honest.** `executor.rs:18938` (`if expected != Some(libc::EACCES) || supervisor_is_nonroot`) and `executor.rs:19597` (`if geteuid() != 0`) skip *native-oracle* rows whose expected value is DAC-sensitive. The guest assertions in the same loops (`18945-18956`, `19687-19691`) are unconditional, the create-directory native oracle at `18958-18967` is unconditional, and `supervisor-euid.txt` records EUID 212630, so zero rows were skipped in the recorded run. The `19597` guard additionally prevents a root test run from actually mutating the host's `/proc/uptime` mode (procfs `proc_notify_change` permits root `chmod`). Each changed production gate has a failing causal mutation: removing `F_SEAL_WRITE` from `SYNTHETIC_PROC_REQUIRED_SEALS`, reintroducing the legacy `ELOOP` arm, replacing the trailing-slash `EISDIR` with `ENOENT`, and deleting the stale-key `remove`. I read all four isolated patches and logs; all four are one-hunk, semantically targeted, and produce the intended literal failure (`0x7` vs the seal mask; `-40` vs `-20`; `-ENOENT` vs `-EISDIR`; retained forbidden marker). The seal mutation is the strongest: the expected mask in `executor.rs:29579-29580` is recomputed in the test rather than read from the production constant, so a producer/validator co-mutation cannot hide it.

## Conclusions by area

**Sealed-carrier integrity — sound, and it closes a real base defect.** At base, `open_synthetic_proc` (`base/.../executor.rs:12828-12859`) inserted the `memfd_create` descriptor itself into the guest table, so the 17 fixed `/proc` snapshots were exposed `O_RDWR`, unsealed, and mode ~0755 — `write`, `ftruncate`, and `fchmod` on a "read-only" `/proc/uptime` fd would have gone through. (The base test at `base/.../executor.rs:17895` only checked that a *writable open* was refused, never `write` on the read-only-opened fd.) At head, `executor.rs:13124-13201` creates with `MFD_CLOEXEC|MFD_ALLOW_SEALING`, writes the content, `fchmod`s to `0o444`, adds `F_SEAL_WRITE|GROW|SHRINK|SEAL`, re-reads and requires exactly that mask or that mask plus `F_SEAL_EXEC`, then opens `/proc/self/fd/<construction>` `O_RDONLY` (or `O_PATH`) and `drop`s the construction handle at `13189` before `insert_file_with_flags` at `13191`. Every early return drops the construction `File`; `insert_file_with_flags` retires the file on `EMFILE` or identity-allocation failure. `F_SEAL_WRITE` cannot fail with `EBUSY` here because no shared writable mapping exists. I traced the write vectors: `write`/`writev` → `ensure_writable` → `EBADF` (`5264-5275`); `pwrite64` → the `proc_files` arm at `5759-5772`; `ftruncate` → `EINVAL` at `6791-6796`; `fchmod` → `EPERM` at `12332-12338`; `mmap MAP_SHARED|PROT_WRITE` → `EACCES` at `14369-14371`; guest proc-fd reopen → `EACCES`/`EINVAL` at `7499-7510`. The one path that reaches a host `O_RDWR` description is an SCM_RIGHTS round-trip (`received_proc_inode` returns `None` for a memfd, so the received fd loses its `proc_files` classification and the `regular_proc` gate no longer applies); under a root supervisor the mode-0444 check would not stop the reopen either — and this is exactly the case the seal exists for: the write then fails `EPERM` in the kernel. Defence in depth holds.

**Determinism — preserved, with one new host-dependent surface.** Content bytes are unchanged; the carrier is now immutable, which strictly increases determinism. `sanitize_proc_stat`/`synthetic_proc_statx` (`13301-13366`) still zero all timestamps and substitute the FNV-1a inode and synthetic dev, and the removal of the base `lseek(0)` is compensated by the fresh description starting at offset 0. The new nondeterminism surface is host-kernel dependence (finding 2). The SCM_RIGHTS declassification noted above also drops the guest back to the raw memfd inode — pre-existing, and covered by the disclosed SCM_RIGHTS-identity nonclaim.

**Linux semantics — materially improved and, where I could check against pinned source, correct.** Verified directly against `linux/`: the `O_PATH`-beats-everything reduction (`v7.1-fs-open.c:1170-1172`) is now modelled by `LEGACY_O_PATH_FLAGS` (`executor.rs:197-198`, `7167-7171`), which also fixes `uses_mode`/`named_create` for `O_PATH|O_CREAT`; `invalid_legacy_tmpfile_flags` (`201-210`) reproduces `v6.3-fs-open.c:1204-1209`'s `O_TMPFILE_MASK` test exactly, including the `ACC_MODE(3)` write-capable case; `ksys_pwrite64`'s `pos<0 → EINVAL` before `fdget`, then `EBADF`, then `FMODE_PWRITE → ESPIPE` (`v6.3-fs-read_write.c:686-704`) is reproduced at `executor.rs:5747-5772`, and `seq_open` clearing `FMODE_PWRITE` (`v6.3-fs-seq_file.c:76-85`) justifies `ESPIPE` for the 15 seq-file paths while `/proc/self/cmdline` and `/proc/sys/kernel/osrelease` correctly give `EBADF` via `vfs_write`'s `FMODE_WRITE` check. `synthetic_proc_every_regular_surface_matches_native_pwrite_result` (`18060-18115`) is a genuine oracle — it derives the expectation from the production classifier and then compares against a real host `pwrite` on each of the 17 paths, and `final-native-open-matrix.log:2-18` independently records the same 15×ESPIPE / 2×EBADF split. `ftruncate` on `O_PATH` correctly yields `EBADF` (kernel `fdget` masks `FMODE_PATH`) and `EINVAL` for a live non-writable regular description. The low-32-bit fd decoding now matches `unsigned int fd` for `pwrite64`, `ftruncate`, `fchmod`, and `mmap`.

**Lifecycle and locking — no regression found.** `FdinfoDescription::observe` (`1736-1803`) keeps the documented seq → one file table → lifecycle order and takes no new locks; `ensure_fdinfo_content_supported` (`2008-2025`) explicitly avoids locking `fdinfo_table`, which is safe because `open_file` holds exclusive `&mut state`. Every refusal in `open_fdinfo` precedes `open_synthetic_proc`, so no carrier, sequence state, or table entry is allocated on failure — pinned by `assert_fdinfo_rejection_does_not_allocate` (`29344-29400`), which snapshots `files`, `fd_entry_ids`, and `fdinfo_files` keys around each rejected open. The generation binding survives leader exit with a live worker (`31562-31680`), including with `LegacyLookup` injected after the leader dies, and dead-parent `ENOENT` correctly precedes the legacy create errors. `synthetic_proc_nofollow_fds` is propagated through `dup`/`dup2`/`dup3`/`F_DUPFD`, cleared on `close`, filtered on exec, copied on fork, and round-trips through `FileTableState` — all asserted at `19259-19350`. The carrier fd can never collide with an fdinfo `target_fd`, since `target_fd` must be live for the open to proceed.

## Residual and nonclaim audit

Accurately bounded, and none of them invalidates the narrower claims actually made:

- **Generic virtual-file carriers unsealed and writable through proc-fd** (`/proc/self/loginuid`, `/dev/urandom`, one cpufreq path). Confirmed real: `open_virtual_file` (`base` and head, `executor.rs:7046-7083`-equivalent) omits `MFD_ALLOW_SEALING` and leaves the default memfd mode, and the new test proves a successful `O_RDWR` reopen and 1-byte write. The claim is limited to exactly the three sampled paths; the report says so. Determinism is not broken — the mutation is a deterministic function of guest actions on a per-open carrier — and native `/proc/self/loginuid` is genuinely writable, so this is a fidelity gap of bounded consequence.
- **Fdinfo `O_PATH` (including `O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW`) remains `ENOSYS`; bare fdinfo `O_CREAT`, `O_CREAT|O_EXCL`, `O_TRUNC`, `O_DIRECT` ordering mismatched.** Confirmed at `executor.rs:2050-2060`. Accurately stated.
- **Exact `/proc/self/fdinfo/` ordinary open / `O_DIRECTORY` / `O_TMPFILE` remains `ENOENT`.** Confirmed: base already returned `ENOENT` for the empty suffix, and `FdinfoPathTarget::EmptyFinal` preserves it at `7076`. Only the legacy create-directory arm changes. Accurately scoped. I also found an *undisclosed* sibling of the same class: `/proc/self/fdinfo/<n>/` (trailing slash after a numeric leaf) parses as `MissingFinal` → `ENOENT` where Linux gives `ENOTDIR` (`executor.rs:1975-1985`). Pre-existing, identical in base, immaterial.
- **Proc-fd `O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW` fail-closed as `ELOOP`.** Confirmed at `7472-7474` and `7485-7491`, and the test at `19693-19707` asserts the native result is success while the guest deliberately refuses. Honestly labelled as fail-closed, not as parity.
- **Direct `/proc/mounts` `O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW` link identity.** Confirmed divergent: `open_file:7102` skips the `ELOOP` arm for `O_PATH`, so the guest gets an `O_PATH` handle to the memfd and `fstat` reports `S_IFREG 0444` where Linux reports the symlink. Disclosed.
- **Fdinfo statx truncated mask.** Confirmed exactly: `synthetic_proc_statx:13342-13349` yields `0x71f`, omitting `STATX_ATIME|MTIME|CTIME` from the requested `0x7ff`. `executor.rs:29512-29522` asserts the native side reports the full mask and the guest does not — the mismatch is pinned as a mismatch, not as parity.
- **Credential-exact root mutation parity not claimed.** Confirmed and substantiated: root can `chmod` a procfs PDE via `proc_notify_change`, so the guest's unconditional `EPERM` at `12332-12338` genuinely diverges under a root supervisor. The real-KVM guest proves `getuid()==geteuid()==0` immediately before requiring `EPERM` (patch 4692-4695), so the divergence is explicit rather than hidden.
- **Future implicit seal → `EOPNOTSUPP`.** Confirmed at `13165-13167` and pinned by `synthetic_proc_seal_policy_accepts_only_supported_kernel_shapes` using a reserved `0x40` bit.
- **No 5.8–6.3 runtime.** Confirmed: `installed-modules.txt` and `kernel.txt` show only 6.13.2 / 6.19.2 / 7.1.3, and no artifact claims otherwise. See finding 5.
- **mmap type / `MAP_SHARED_VALIDATE` / later `mprotect(PROT_WRITE)` provenance.** Confirmed out of scope and confirmed harmless to the safety claim: the backend copies file-backed mappings into guest memory (`executor.rs:14376+`), so even a wrongly-permitted writable mapping cannot mutate the carrier.
- **Prerequisite only — no syncfs, no SCM_RIGHTS carrier identity, no identity marker, no record/replay, no full parity.** Confirmed by inspection of the whole diff: nothing in the 4,137/209 change adds any of these.

One residual is *not* disclosed and should be: finding 2 (host-kernel-dependent errno).
